probes.why: the cosmetic path calls ten engine functions and reasons about nine more, and a detour on any of them means W2-C dresses a player through somebody else's code and reports success -- the silent wrong-avatar failure this packet exists to remove. tests/identity/sitecheck.py already reads all of them out of echovr.exe ON DISK; a detour lands in the mapped image, not in the file, which is exactly why W1-C's first real sweep was refused by rlay.dll. This probe re-reads the same sites, plus the three byte-shape windows the hand-declared structs rest on (the 3<<4 customisation slot stride and the two ActorComponentRef field positions, neither of which any single instruction encodes), out of the image the loader actually mapped. A known-answer control runs first, so a comparison that always agreed cannot report a green it did not earn.
